steps.title: Gather materials and reagents
steps.instruction: Collect all listed items: 15 mL screw‑cap glass vials (Kesell, cat BLP025), 200 µL gel pipette tips (Fisher, cat 13‑611‑116), thick black construction paper, Coumarin 540A dye (Exciton, cat 05450), LDS 798 dye (Exciton, cat 07980), Rhodamine 590 dye (Exciton, cat 05901), Fluorescein sodium salt (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat 30181‑100MG), chloroform (Fisher, HPLC grade, cat C607‑1), deuterated chloroform (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat 151858‑10x0.75 mL), dimethyl sulfoxide (Fisher, ACS grade, cat 151874‑10x0.75), methanol (Fisher, HPLC grade, cat A452‑4), and the three dye solutions prepared as described in the Recipes section.

steps.title: Prepare LDS 798 solution
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL screw‑cap glass vial dissolve 0.10 mg LDS 798 in 0.75 mL chloroform, add 1.5 mL deuterated chloroform, stir overnight on a magnetic stirrer; the resulting solution should have an optical density ≈1.2 at 594 nm (≈10⁻⁴ M) and be stored in the dark at room temperature for ≥2 months.

steps.title: Prepare Coumarin 540A solution
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL screw‑cap glass vial dissolve 0.15 mg Coumarin 540A in 3.3 mL DMSO; the solution should have an optical density ≈0.6 at 427 nm (≈10⁻⁴ M) and be stored in the dark at room temperature for ≥2 months.

steps.title: Prepare Rhodamine 590 solution
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL screw‑cap glass vial dissolve 0.05 mg Rhodamine 6G in 10 mL methanol; the solution should have an optical density ≈0.3 at 528 nm (≈10⁻⁵ M) and be stored in the dark at room temperature for ≥4 months.

steps.title: Build optical setup for two‑photon measurements
steps.instruction: On the optical table place the femtosecond laser and the PC1 spectrofluorimeter ≈2 m apart, then remove the excitation lamp, the mirror holder with its two mirrors, the two lens tubes, the optional beam splitter and optional filter from the excitation path; keep the empty second tube entering the sample compartment; insert 3‑mm cuvette adaptors into the Sample and Reference cuvette holders; add a 25‑mm adaptor with a 770/SP short‑pass filter to the Left Emission Channel; disconnect the Left Emission Wavelength stepper‑motor cable; install a spare 4‑slot motorized filter wheel with New Focus ND filters (OD = 1 in slot 1, OD = 0.5 in slot 2, OD = 0.3 in slot 3, slot 4 empty) into the excitation path and connect its stepper motor to the Left Emission Wavelength motor jack; place the excitation polarizer into the optical path; turn on PC1 and its control computer.

steps.title: Create VINCI Power Dependence template
steps.instruction: In VINCI software open Experiment → Single Point → Intensity; remove the Fixed Parameter block for Left Emission Wavelength; add a Variable Parameter block for Left Emission Wavelength; name the filters #1‑0.1T, #2‑0.3T, #3‑0.5T, #4‑empty; set Time Base to 10 s, Number of Iterations to 1; save as “Power Dependence”.

steps.title: Create VINCI Spectral Scan template
steps.instruction: In VINCI open Experiment → Slow Kinetics → Intensity; add a Variable Parameter block for Sample; set Time Base to 1.0 s; set Variable Parameters start = 0 s, stop = 6500 s, step = 6.00; set ‘Measure Dark every’ to 200 min; in Fixed Parameters set Left Emission Wavelength to empty; save as “Spectral Scan”.

steps.title: Align laser and set initial power
steps.instruction: Turn on the laser in alignment mode (200 mW) at 720 nm wearing safety goggles; set mirror M1 to deflect the beam 90° horizontally; place a half‑wave plate (fast axis ≈45°) and a Glan Laser polarizer (vertical axis) in rotation mounts after M1; use mirrors M2‑M4 to bring the beam to the PC1 entrance aperture, adjusting height with M2‑M3 and centering with M3‑M4; insert the continuously variable ND filter after M3, then a flip mirror (FM) after M4 (flipped up); place a power meter after the flip mirror; set the ND filter wheel to maximum transmission and verify ~200 mW; then attenuate to ~20 mW; open the excitation shutter in VINCI, set Left Emission Wavelength to position 4 (empty); align the beam along the axis from the PC1 entrance aperture to the sample‑holder window using M3‑M4; insert a 45‑mm achromatic lens into a 22‑to‑25 mm adaptor tube, slide the adaptor over the 22‑mm tube in the sample compartment, ensure the beam still hits the centre of the sample‑holder opening, re‑align if needed, then turn off the laser.

steps.title: Connect laser to LabView and set 850 nm
steps.instruction: Disconnect the laser from the InSight GUI and connect it via RS‑232 to a PC running the custom LabView program; launch the program, turn on the laser, tune to 850 nm, flip the flip mirror up, open the laser shutter, ensure the continuously variable ND filter is fully transmitting, then slowly rotate the half‑wave plate until the power reads 200 mW; lock this half‑wave plate position for future use.

steps.title: Calibrate ND filter transmission vs wavelength
steps.instruction: Place the power‑meter sensor in the sample compartment (centered in the excitation opening) and set the excitation polarizer to horizontal (90°) via VINCI; rotate the external Glan Laser polarizer to minimise power and lock its position; slide the excitation polarizer out of the beam; for each wavelength in the list 680, 690, 710, 730, 780, 800, 810, 840, 900, 940, 960, 1000, 1050, 1060, 1100, 1200, 1300 nm, set the laser to that wavelength, change the Left Emission Wavelength filter wheel from positions 1‑3 to position 4, record the power for each position, compute the ratio of power (positions 1‑3)/(position 4); store all ratios in an Origin workbook as a calibration table.

steps.title: Prepare emission path and cuvette holders
steps.instruction: Insert a 770/SP filter into a 22‑to‑25 mm adaptor tube and place it over the 22‑mm tube in the left emission collection path; load Semrock 633/SP, 694/SP, and 680/SP filters into the Left Emission Filter Wheel slots 1‑3 (slot 4 empty); remove the two adaptor holders for 3 × 3 mm cuvettes, attach a 0.9 × 4 cm black paper strip to the side with the four screws leaving a ≈0.7 mm slit on the left side of each holder, re‑mount the holders and secure the paper with the screws.

steps.title: Prepare sample and reference solutions for measurement
steps.instruction: Prepare up to two new sample solutions and reference solutions (LDS 798 and Coumarin 540A) as described in the Recipes; add 150 µL of each solution to separate 3 × 3 mm optical cuvettes; measure absorption spectra with a Lambda 950 spectrophotometer, adjusting concentration so that the optical density at the spectral maximum is between 0.2 and 1.5; place magnetic stir bars in the reference cuvettes.

steps.title: Initial instrument setup for Coumarin 540A measurement
steps.instruction: Load Coumarin 540A solution into the Sample holder; ensure Left Emission Channel contains filters 770/SP and 633/SP; turn on the laser at full power, start the LabView control program, turn on PC1; insert the adaptor holders for 3 × 3 mm cuvettes into Sample and Reference positions, keeping the masked side toward the left emission channel; start stirring both Sample and Reference; manually set the left emission wavelength wheel to position 1 (633/SP); insert the left emission polarizer and set it to the Magic Angle via VINCI; set laser wavelength to 800 nm, adjust ND filter to ~20 mW, flip the flip mirror down to send the beam to PC1, remove the excitation polarizer from the beam, set the excitation ND filter wheel to empty (slot 4), open the excitation shutter; in a dark room with the sample‑compartment lid removed, slide the 45‑mm lens adaptor along the 22‑mm tube to maximize fluorescence intensity on the left PMT, then fix its position with a small screw.

steps.title: Adjust power range for samples #1 and #2
steps.instruction: Select the appropriate short‑pass filter (770/SP, 633/SP, 680/SP, 694/SP, or empty) so its cutoff exceeds the fluorescence peak of the sample; replace the Coumarin 540A cuvette with sample #1, close the compartment lid, measure the maximum signal at several wavelengths across the 2PA spectrum (e.g., 700, 800, 900, 1000, 1100, 1200 nm) using the left PMT; repeat for sample #2; adjust the continuous ND filter for each sample so that the maximum signal across the spectrum is ≈1 × 10⁶ counts (typically requiring 10–100 mW depending on concentration and two‑photon brightness).

steps.title: Check power‑dependence quadratic behavior
steps.instruction: Using the Power Dependence VINCI file, record fluorescence versus laser power for each sample at short‑wavelength steps of 20 nm (e.g., 680, 700, 720 nm, …); fit the data to a power law and confirm the exponent lies between 1.95 and 2.05 (quadratic); identify the shortest wavelength where the response is quadratic for each sample.

steps.title: Scan two‑photon spectra of samples #1 and #2
steps.instruction: Place sample #1 cuvette in the Sample position and sample #2 cuvette in the Reference position; set the start wavelength of the laser scan to the shortest quadratic wavelength found in the previous step; determine the stop wavelength by doubling the longest wavelength observed in the one‑photon absorption edge and rounding to the nearest value in the series 680, ...; set step size to 4 nm and dwell time to 42 s; open the Spectral Scan VINCI file, enter experiment notes (sample names, positions, filters), and start the scan; after completion, remove the cuvettes.

steps.title: Scan two‑photon spectrum of Coumarin 540A
steps.instruction: Insert two identical Coumarin 540A cuvettes (in DMSO) into Sample and Reference positions; set the stop wavelength to 980 nm; keep all other Spectral Scan settings as in the previous step and run the scan; record notes accordingly.

steps.title: Scan two‑photon spectrum of LDS 798
steps.instruction: Insert two identical LDS 798 cuvettes (CHCl₃/CDCl₃ 1:2) into Sample and Reference positions; set the left emission filter wheel to empty (slot 4); set the start wavelength to 940 nm; keep all other Spectral Scan parameters as before and run the scan; record notes.

steps.title: Import raw spectral data into OriginLab
steps.instruction: In OriginLab create an Import Wizard (File → Import → Import Wizard) that reads the .ifx file and produces columns ‘Time’, ‘Sample’, ‘Intensity’, ‘IntensityStdError’, ‘Real time’; name the wizard “2PA_sample_and_reference”.

steps.title: Create auto‑analysis script filter
steps.instruction: Using the Import Wizard, add an auto‑analysis script filter named “2PA_sample_and_reference_autocalculation”; paste Script 1 from the supplemental file into the “Script after each file imported” window; specify the first wavelength, last wavelength, wavelength step, and seconds per step; after import the workbook should match Figure 14 and a verification graph (Figure 16) should appear showing two distinct spectra; if outlier points appear, manually sort the data.

steps.title: Generate correction functions from reference dyes
steps.instruction: If the measured samples are reference dyes, copy the correct reference spectra into column D (Sample holder) and column E (Reference holder) so that wavelength ranges match; columns F and G become correction functions (raw spectra divided by reference spectra). Merge the short‑range correction functions: normalize each short‑range function by dividing by the mean of its values in the 940‑980 nm range; compute the mean of the two normalized functions in that range and use it as the correction for 940‑980 nm; assemble a full‑range correction function by inserting the Coumarin 540A‑derived function for λ < 936 nm, the averaged 940‑980 nm function, and the LDS 798‑derived function for λ > 980 nm (treat Sample and Reference holders separately).

steps.title: Apply correction to unknown samples
steps.instruction: For unknown samples, copy the previously generated correction functions into columns D (Sample) and E (Reference) so that wavelength ranges align; columns F and G now contain the corrected two‑photon spectra (raw divided by correction).

steps.title: Measure two‑photon cross‑section of red fluorescent protein
steps.instruction: Prepare a Rhodamine 6G stock in methanol; adjust its OD at 528 nm in a 3 × 3 mm cuvette to 0.2–0.3 and record the exact value; adjust the protein sample OD (same cuvette size) to 0.2–0.3 and record; set laser wavelength to 1060 nm; in the Right Emission Channel insert the polarizer and set to Magic Angle via VINCI; set the right emission monochromator to 600 nm and insert two 2‑mm slits; place the Rhodamine 590 cuvette in the Sample holder, adjust the laser power (using the continuous ND filter) so that the right emission intensity is 5 × 10⁴–1 × 10⁵ counts with the excitation filter wheel empty (slot 4), record this power; repeat the power adjustment for the protein sample; run the Power Dependence VINCI file with registration in the Right Emission Channel for both reference and sample; plot fluorescence versus power², fit linear slopes, and compute the ratio of slopes F₂,S/F₂,R; calculate concentration ratio C_R/C_S using OD and extinction coefficients (C_R/C_S = OD_R · ε_S / (OD_S · ε_R)); measure one‑photon fluorescence at 530 nm (excitation slit = 5 nm, emission slit = 16 nm) for both sample and reference to obtain F₁,R(600) and F₁,S(600); compute quantum‑yield ratio φ_R/φ_S = [F₁,R(600)/F₁,S(600)] · [OD_S(530)/OD_R(530)]; finally calculate the sample’s two‑photon cross‑section using σ₂,S = σ₂,R · (F₂,S/F₂,R) · (C_R/C_S) · (φ_R/φ_S) with σ₂,R(1060 nm) = 10 GM.
